Verdict

No confirmed indicators of a malicious supply-chain compromise. Overall risk: **info**.

Malicious Supply-Chain Indicators

No confirmed malicious supply-chain indicators.

Automatic Execution Paths

  • In the provided extracted corpus, there is no evidence of .pth, sitecustomize.py, usercustomize.py, setup.py, clearly malicious PEP 517 build hooks, or install-time automatic execution.
  • docker/Dockerfile contains ENTRYPOINT ["conda", ..., "badger"] and adds conda activation to ~/.bashrc, but this appears to be container/development environment setup, not a malicious PyPI install-time execution path.
  • Normal CLI/GUI behavior and plugin installation logic that requires user action were not treated as malicious automatic execution evidence.

Theft / Exfiltration / Persistence / Lateral Movement / Obfuscation

  • **Credential theft:** No evidence of broad harvesting of environment variables, .env files, SSH keys, cloud credentials, CI tokens, wallet files, or similar secrets.
  • **Network/exfiltration:** src/badger/actions/install.py contains requests.get() and plugin download logic, but the function currently prints a disabled-message and returns near the start. The code appears to be user-triggered plugin management functionality, with no evidence of credential theft or uploads to attacker-controlled C2.
  • **Archive/staging:** tarfile.open(..., "r:gz") and tar.extractall(...) are used for plugin tarball handling. There is no evidence tying this to sensitive-file collection, staging, compression, or exfiltration.
  • **Persistence:** Dockerfile line RUN echo "source activate badger" > ~/.bashrc is conda environment auto-activation inside a container. No host persistence via cron, systemd, launch agents, shell-profile backdoors, or similar mechanisms was confirmed.
  • **Lateral movement:** No evidence of Kubernetes abuse, Docker socket access, cloud metadata access, GitHub Actions token theft, workflow injection, or CI/cloud lateral movement patterns.
  • **Obfuscation/loaders:** Some eval/exec usage is present, but in the context of mathematical expression evaluation, dtype conversion, GUI message parsing, or plugin metadata detection. No evidence of base64/zlib/marshal-hidden payloads, staged downloader stubs, RAT payload selection, or self-deleting droppers was found.

Distribution Integrity Anomalies

  • Many PNG files were flagged as high-entropy, but their paths and names match documentation/screenshot assets. No hidden payload or unexplained native binary was confirmed.
  • Based on the provided data, there is no confirmed PyPI-vs-source mismatch, sudden dependency insertion, typosquatting evidence, or wheel/sdist behavior mismatch.

Additional Verification Needed

  • Only selected text from 321 files was reviewed. Further review of unprovided files, full build configuration (pyproject.toml, setup.cfg, etc.), package entry points, and included data files would be needed for higher confidence.
  • No comparison was provided between the PyPI sdist and the official GitHub source tag/release, so distribution-integrity assessment is limited.
  • Large PNG/binary files were not content-analyzed here; if concerns remain, file magic, metadata, and steganography checks can be performed separately.
